## 1. 当前观察 (observation)

### Scope, units and statistics

- **Seed scope.** Seeds 3401 (breadth seed; the published ADDENDUM_05 units), 3407 and 3413 (ADDENDUM_03 panel rows, registered before any of them ran; panel rows and counterparts per seed: 3401 85, 3407 85, 3413 85). Panel configurations (17): E_GENERIC {NCE, CS_SINGLE} × {cbramod, reve} × {random_full, pretrained_peft, pretrained_full}; E_LOCAL lag_local_tokens full (NCE, CS_SINGLE); E_PUBLIC_TRANSFER source lag_local_tokens task_partial (NCE, CS_SINGLE); E_GX GX_NATIVE full. Every other E configuration keeps its seed-3401-only statement (see 'Not in the panel').
- **Children.** 64 children (HA 55, NH 9), each tested in one of 5 subject folds (content fold 0); the children and per-child trial counts of every fold are identical across the 17 configurations and the three seeds. Expected children per family: 64; missing pairs: 0. n counts children; seeds and folds never add n.
- **Endpoints, kept separate.** Calibrated NLL = positive-affine calibrated natural-distribution NLL (bits per trial; ΔNLL = reference − candidate). AUC = positive-affine `auc_score` (= native ranking; ΔAUC = candidate − reference). History increment = `hist_gain_bits` (EEG added to the declared history model q_hist, bits per trial; Δ = candidate − reference). Twin sensitivity = history increment − the increment of the null-twin EEG (a same-record, same-history-bin trial from another block). Positive = candidate better throughout. NLL and the history increments are printed with 4 decimals, AUC with 3.
- **Contrasts.** The frozen ADDENDUM_05 §5 families restricted, by design, to the members whose reference and candidate are both panel configurations (PE-GENERIC 2 of 4 members per scope, PE-LOCAL 7 of 16, PE-TRANSFER 1 of 6; PE-COMPLEMENT and PE-DISTILL have no panel rows). The PE-TRANSFER member and the PE-LOCAL member `transfer/lag_local_tokens/task_partial` are the same paired difference in two families. Tag `recipe (C01)`: `random_full → pretrained_full` is a recipe contrast (CORRECTION_01): the initialisation changes together with the learning-rate cell; in the private records the backbone learning rate of pretrained_full is 3× to 100× lower than that of random_full and the head learning rate differs in 3 of 4 scopes; the epochs are the same; both arms train every backbone parameter from the start (§1.16). The frozen code's tag 'initialization (matched full update)' is kept in the JSON as `frozen_tag`. `random_full → pretrained_peft` changes the initialisation, the trainable parameters (LoRA adapters) and the learning rates. PE-LOCAL and PE-TRANSFER compare different declared input access (E_LOCAL local_only 0–600 ms; E_GENERIC zero-padded −200…600 ms epoch; E_PUBLIC_TRANSFER private_task_declared_input): access-extended comparisons, not pure architecture contrasts.
- **Intervals.** Bootstrap-t over children (B = 4,000); [sim.] = simultaneous 95 % by max-t within the panel family, for NLL and AUC separately (the frozen families). In the one-member PE-TRANSFER families the simultaneous interval equals the pointwise one. Replicate indices depend only on the frozen label, the metric and n, so the three seeds and the identity mean resample the same children (whole seed vectors jointly). Identity mean = per child, the mean over seeds of the within-seed paired difference; its intervals use the same families. History increment and twin sensitivity: pointwise 95 % (frozen secondaries); the history increment also gets a max-t within the same family (addition A, exploratory). Classes (I>0 / I<0 / contains 0) describe simultaneous intervals of the declared draws; §1.14 shows their Monte-Carlo stability. No p-values.
- **Uncertainty scope.** Intervals condition on the fitted models. The between-seed range and SD are the only direct view of training randomness, and three seeds give a coarse one. The seed changes initialisation and batch order, the training-side target statistics and calibration batches, E_GENERIC heads and adaptation (`random_full` also re-draws the backbone), and the E_PUBLIC_TRANSFER donor (donor seed = target seed); the early-stopping blocks, the folds and the E_GENERIC learning rates (chosen once on the seed-3401 development cell, §1.16) do not change. The same children are reused, so agreement across seeds is not an independent replication.

### 1.15 Unit-level description (exploratory, descriptive: post hoc addition F, version 2, declared after version 1 had been read; post hoc addition G, version 3, declared after version 2 had been read)

Unit = one trained record (configuration × seed × subject fold, 12–13 test children). Values are means over the unit's test children; the calibrator slope is the unit's training-side positive-affine fit (comparable only within a configuration). No intervals; every unit of every panel configuration is listed (folds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 in order).

The E_GENERIC learning rates are the `chosen` pair of the ALN2 private recipe search named in each record (`auditory_alignment_v2.run_fm.lr_select`: candidates trained on one development cell, scored by the checkpoint-selection score on the training participants' early-stopping content; the chosen pair is fixed for every fold and seed). `local_train.fit_private_fm` (E_GENERIC) trains one backbone parameter group and one head group with AdamW (weight decay 1e-4) and cosine annealing over all steps: no progressive prefix, no layer-wise decay. ## 2. 当前工作判断 (working interpretation)

These are working judgements for this panel only: 17 private-task configurations, seeds 3401 / 3407 / 3413, the same 64 children
(HA 55, NH 9). They are not final conclusions. Sections 2–4, 6 and 7 were written by hand after the version-2 tables had been viewed
(version 1 was read 00:11–00:14, the §1.15 table at 00:18 CEST). In version 3 they were corrected by hand after an independent
verification of version 2 and after the version-3 tables (01:09 and 01:13 CEST) had been viewed; every correction is listed with its
version-2 wording in section 7. The file's modification time marks the end of the version-3 edits. All AUC differences are in AUC units, all
NLL and history-increment differences in bits per trial.

1. **Ranking (AUC) reproduces across seeds; calibrated NLL reproduces except for REVE CS_SINGLE.**
   - AUC levels move by at most 0.014 between seeds (largest: NCE reve pretrained_peft 0.520 / 0.529 / 0.515). For every one of the 24 AUC
     members the between-seed spread is below every per-seed simultaneous width (§1.13).
   - The NLL levels of 14 of the 17 configurations lie within 0.714–0.718 in every seed, with between-seed spreads ≤ 0.0014.
   - The three REVE CS_SINGLE configurations are the exception: random_full 0.811 / 0.723 / 0.736, pretrained_peft 0.722 / 0.911 / 0.927,
     pretrained_full 0.719 / 0.732 / 0.720. Their AUC stays at 0.499–0.533.
   - The unit table (§1.15; post hoc additions F and G) shows two patterns. NLL excess = unit NLL − the median unit NLL of the 14 reference
     configurations (every panel configuration except the three REVE CS_SINGLE ones) in the same seed and fold; over those 210 reference
     units it lies in −0.005 … +0.003.
     - The three large failures raise every unit of their seed: random_full 3401 +0.081 … +0.111 (unit NLL 0.7924–0.8295), pretrained_peft
       3407 +0.133 … +0.266 (0.8421–0.9862) and pretrained_peft 3413 +0.151 … +0.239 (0.8707–0.9563).
     - In the moderately raised seed cells the rise is uneven across the five units: random_full 3407 (level 0.723) +0.002 … +0.009, with
       fold 0 inside the reference range; random_full 3413 (0.736) +0.0579 / +0.0014 / +0.0075 / +0.0239 / +0.0042, with fold 1 inside the
       reference range; pretrained_full 3407 (0.732) +0.0393 / +0.0122 / +0.0047 / +0.0161 / +0.0035, all five above the largest reference
       excess (+0.0028), two of them by less than 0.002 and one by 0.036.
     - In the other three REVE CS_SINGLE seed cells (pretrained_peft 3401, pretrained_full 3401 and 3413), 0–2 of the five units lie above the
       largest reference excess (at most +0.016).
   - For REVE CS_SINGLE the calibrated NLL is therefore mainly a question of how the probability calibration transfers to new children,
     not of ranking.
2. **Generic FM recipes against random_full (PE-GENERIC; recipe contrasts, CORRECTION_01).**

## 3. 仍竞争的解释 (competing explanations)

- **REVE CS_SINGLE calibration failures.** The present records do not separate these explanations:
  - (a) **In-sample self-matching in the CS_SINGLE score.** Reading `calib.private_variants` (CS_SINGLE branch; read only, part of the
    hashed private code):
    - the class-kernel reference set (up to 6,000 trials, drawn with `default_rng(seed + 77)`) is taken from the same training
      early-stopping blocks on which the positive-affine calibrator is then fitted;
    - so about 80 % of the calibration trials (6,000 of 7,411–7,604) contain their own label at kernel weight 1, while test children never do;
    - where the other kernel weights are small, the calibration scores separate the classes far better than the test scores, the fitted
      slope becomes steep, and the test NLL rises above the base-rate entropy;
    - test-child ranking (AUC) is unaffected, which fits the stable AUC.
    - The size of the effect depends on the bandwidth relative to the representation's spread, which differs between trained units. It
      would act on every CS_SINGLE unit, but it is visible only where the representation carries little ranking information. Not
      quantified here.
  - (b) **A seed-level training state shared by the five folds.** Within one seed every fold starts from the same random draws: the
    random_full initialisation, the PEFT adapter, the batch order and the calibration and kernel samples. This fits the three large
    failures, in which all five units of the seed are raised (§1.15, addition G). It fits the moderately raised seed cells less well: there
    the excess differs strongly between the units of one seed (random_full 3413: +0.058 in fold 0, +0.001 in fold 1).
  - (c) **A generally fragile REVE CS_SINGLE readout.** The 3401 interim already had the outlier. CBraMod CS_SINGLE and every NCE arm are stable.
  - **What the unit table shows (§1.15).** Within pretrained_peft and pretrained_full, the high-NLL seeds tend to have the steeper
    calibrators (pretrained_peft slopes 0.14–0.41 at 3401, 3.1–3.3 at 3407 and 1.5–2.1 at 3413; pretrained_full up to 0.79 at 3407 against
    ≤ 0.362 elsewhere). Within random_full the slopes are steep at every seed (4.1–9.8), but the NLL is high mainly at 3401 (unit means
    0.792–0.829), so the slope alone does not explain the pattern.
  - The records hold no per-trial scores. They do hold, per child, the uncalibrated class-kernel NLL next to the positive-affine NLL, which
    allows a first check without new computation (§4.1).
- **PEFT / full gains over random_full.** These are recipe contrasts (CORRECTION_01): the pretrained weights change together with the
  learning-rate cell, and for PEFT with the trainable parameters. Optimiser, schedule and epochs are the same within a backbone (§1.16).
  - Part of the gain may come from random_full being a weak recipe at this data size: it is below the local model in every scope.
  - No matched-initialisation contrast exists for the private task (ALN32_TRUE_FULL covers the public tasks only).
- **FM arms at or below the local model.** These explanations are not separated:
  - (a) the ALN2 private FM recipes and the shared readout (`spatial_signed_k8_e32_v1`) may be sub-optimal for this task;
  - (b) the extra pre-stimulus EEG of the padded epoch may add more variance than information;
  - (c) the local lag-token structure may suit event-locked epochs.
- **No transfer effect resolved.** These explanations remain open:
  - (a) the FAU donor's temporal kernels may not carry structure the private class task needs. The 3-sample kernels span 23 ms at 128 Hz but
    12 ms at 250 Hz, as disclosed in `run_transfer`;
  - (b) task_partial freezes the loaded tensors and re-initialises the input map, the lag table and the projection, which may discard what
    the donor learned;
  - (c) a real benefit may exist but be smaller than about 0.01 AUC. Only (c) is directly bounded by the data.
- **History increments at or below 0.** The EEG readout on top of q_hist is an offset logistic fitted on the training children's
  early-stopping blocks. A negative increment on test children can come from overfitting of that readout as well as from a lack of
  current-class information beyond the history. The non-negative twin-sensitivity estimates (true trial EEG at least as good as the
  same-bin twin) argue against "no trial-specific information", but they carry no interval here.
- **Scope.**
  - All intervals are conditional on the fitted models.
  - Three seeds sample training randomness coarsely; a fourth seed can fall outside the observed range.
  - The same 64 children have been analysed in many earlier rounds (brief B01: about 20), so agreement across seeds is not an independent
    replication.

## 4. 下一轮干预 (next intervention)

1. **REVE CS_SINGLE calibration diagnosis.**
   - **(i) CPU, from the existing records** (a new, separately noted exploratory analysis, not run here). Compare, per child and unit, the
     stored uncalibrated class-kernel NLL with the positive-affine NLL for every CS_SINGLE panel unit, REVE and CBraMod alike (90 E_GENERIC
     units plus the E_LOCAL and E_PUBLIC_TRANSFER CS units as references).
     - If the class-kernel NLL stays near the base-rate entropy where the positive-affine NLL fails, the failure lies in the calibrator fit,
       which supports (a).
   - **(ii) GPU, evaluation only, under a new execution version.** Re-score the same units from their checkpoints (all 255 panel `*_best.pt`
     files are present). Store per-trial scores, and form the calibration-set scores with the trial's own entry excluded from the kernel
     reference (leave-one-out).
     - The old values stay; the new ones get a new version.
     - No runner exists yet, so there is no command to report.
2. **A matched-initialisation contrast for the private task**, if the question "does pretraining help the private task" is pursued: a
   TRUE_FULL-style private arm (random and pretrained on the same schedule and learning-rate cell). In the present records random_full
   and pretrained_full already share the optimiser, the schedule, the epochs and the full update of every backbone parameter; besides the
   initialisation they differ in the learning-rate cell (§1.16), so the matched arm mainly needs one shared cell. It needs new IDs and a
   registration first. Not started here.
3. **No automatic extension.** The non-panel members and families (see 'Not in the panel') stay seed-3401-only. Whether they get seed
   panels is a question of resource priority, not a performance gate.
4. **Use as a reference.** The three-seed levels and contrasts here can serve as the reference for the S34_PRIVATE track (current class,
   history and time; package docs/05 §5) once it registers its analyses.
